inline_comments.comment: "the ASE's" contains an extraneous article. Since ASE is a proper acronym, it should read just "ASE's :func:`~ase.io.read` function".

Lines 24–26 are dead RST comment code (`.. or` and `.. >>> view(atoms, repeat=(3, 3, 2))`). The `repeat` example was in the old version and should be either restored as live content or deleted entirely. Leaving it as a hidden comment creates confusion for future contributors and clutters the source.

The underline character for "Selecting a part of a trajectory" was changed from dashes (`---`) to dots (`...`). In RST/Sphinx, heading levels are determined by the order in which underline characters are first encountered in the document. Because dots appear at line 36 before dashes are used at line 59 ("Basic controls"), Sphinx will interpret dots as the *higher* level — making this subsection appear structurally above "Basic controls", "Plotting data from the command line", etc. The heading should use dashes (`---`) to be consistent with the other sections in this file.

The inline comments on lines 54–55 were changed from `# last/first image from all files` to `# last/first image from all .traj files`. This is misleading: the `-n`/`--image-number` flag accepts any file type; `*.traj` is just the glob pattern chosen for the example. The original wording "from all files" was correct. Consider restoring it or rephrasing to "from all matched files" to avoid implying the flag is `.traj`-only.
The blank line inside the `.. attention::` directive (line 6) contains trailing whitespace. This should be a fully empty line.
Trailing whitespace at the end of `"instructions:"` on this line. Should be trimmed.
Grammar error: "These constraints will be then be saved to a file" contains a duplicated "be". Should be "These constraints will then be saved to a file".

Lines 119–121 are a commented-out RST code block (`.. ::` and `..   $ ase gui --interpolate 3 ...`). Dead commented-out content in RST source is invisible to readers and a maintenance burden. Either restore it as an active example under the NEB section, or remove it entirely.

The "Bulk modulus" section body is a single incomplete sentence — `Interface to :func:`ase.eos.plot`` — with no trailing period and no further explanation. At minimum this needs a period, and ideally a sentence explaining what the feature does (e.g., computing an equation of state) so users know what to expect before opening the window.
Typo: "Depending on you operating system" should be "Depending on **your** operating system".

general_comments.comment: The "Writing files" section was entirely removed from `basics.rst` without a replacement or redirect. That section documented the `-o` output flag (e.g., `$ ase gui -n -1 a*.traj -o new.traj`) and listed the supported output formats (`traj`, `xyz`, `cube`, `pdb`, `eps`, `png`, `pov`). This is practically useful information for users who want to convert or export structures via the GUI's command line. Even if the format list is considered outdated, the `-o` flag and a pointer to `ase.io` docs should be preserved somewhere.

In `doc/index.rst`, `gettingstarted/gettingstarted` was moved to appear *after* `ase/ase` (the full API reference). A getting-started guide is typically one of the first things a new user reads; placing it after the complete module reference inverts the expected reading order. Consider whether this reordering was intentional.
